configuration.title: Full or compact, and what to show
configuration.description: The full card shows every part. compact keeps only the picture and the fee, for dense lists: it drops the badges, title, benefits, upsell, and button, so put the card’s name in headline. media replaces the picture in both, for example with an Avatar as Figma’s compact card does. showHeader and showNudge hide the badges and the upsell; showButton hides the button but not its space. Badges take modes, not colours. On the card, AppearanceBrand Secondary turns the benefit icons purple, Badge Size Small makes the badges smaller, and Page type SubPage shows a grey border for white pages; the Button stays small and purple.

states.title: Its button acts, or the whole card does
states.description: The card isn’t pressable: its Apply button is, and a benefit row presses when you give it onPress. onPress makes the whole card one button, named by its title. Use one or the other: a pressable card that keeps its button puts a button inside a button. The card has no disabled, selected, or loading state.

sizing.title: 343 px wide, height from its parts
sizing.description: The card is 343 px wide, as in Figma; width sets another number or a percentage of its host. The height follows the parts you show: 12 px of padding, 8 px between parts, and 12 px between benefits. It comes out taller than Figma’s, because its badges are bigger and its benefits further apart.

content.title: Name the card, then its facts
content.description: Make the title the card’s name, short enough for one line, and the subtitle the kind of card. Give each benefit one fact. Put the fee label in headline, the amount in description, and the billing note in footerSubtitle. Label the button with a verb, such as Apply. Replace every sample: an empty headline, description, or footerSubtitle shows its placeholder word.

sources.title: Use the public CC Card contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Its export is CcCard. Figma’s CC CARD has Compact and Type variants. The package’s card is 264 px tall where Figma’s is 242: its badges are Medium where Figma’s are Small, and its benefits sit 12 px apart instead of 4. Its benefit icons are gold where Figma’s are purple, and its upsell is its own 14 px line instead of Figma’s Nudge. Compact defaults to the 88 × 54 picture where Figma shows a 42 px Avatar, and it drops the title too. The border is white, so it shows only with Page type SubPage. Empty footer text falls back to placeholder words, and the sample badges set their label colour in code. Every published Storybook story renders the card as a pressable button with Apply inside it, and the published page is the older generated one (all reported).
